blockers.summary: ⛔ "No EMC line is in GDSC2" is FALSE against this document's own committed input cache, and it is printed twice — inside the ⛔ banner the document says is repeated in every artifact, and again in §6.2 item 2. The line DepMap labels EMC (ACH-001519 / H-EMC-SS) IS in GDSC2 8.5 and has residual LN_IC50 values for BOTH ATR inhibitors used in part D. The claim is load-bearing: it is the stated reason this assessment "cannot become that evidence at any sample size from any public dataset". The correct fact is already in the paper and is STRONGER — §2 establishes that this line is recorded as not carrying the fusion, so its ATR-inhibitor values are not a readout on an NR4A3 fusion — and a reader who checks the cache finds an unreported ATRi readout on the line the paper calls EMC sitting behind a sentence saying no such data exists.
blockers.evidence: Sentence, verbatim, at manuscript lines 40-41: "no ATR inhibitor has ever been put on an NR4A3-fusion-positive cell. No EMC line is in GDSC2; the one line DepMap labels EMC has no CRISPR data"; repeated at line 749. Refuted by research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json -> part_d.gdsc_residual_ln_ic50_by_drug: ACH-001519 is a key in ALL SEVEN drug maps — azd6738 (ceralasertib) residual -0.0047 in a 956-line map, ve-822 (berzosertib) +2.0477 in an 892-line map, plus paclitaxel -4.0902, olaparib +1.6678, talazoparib -0.7541, mk-1775 -0.87, bortezomib -7.8713. Those two map sizes are the same 956/892 the manuscript prints in §5. emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines ~2645-2676 build that map ONLY from rows of the GDSC2 fitted-dose-response table (gdsc_meta.source "GDSC2_8.5_27Oct23", n_rows 242036) whose SANGER_MODEL_ID/COSMIC_ID maps to a DepMap model, and the residual is LN_IC50 minus that line's own GDSC median — so a value cannot exist for a line absent from GDSC2. That ACH-001519 is the EMC-labelled line is the paper's own citation: research/modalities/fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> emc_line = {model_id ACH-001519, oncotree_label "Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma", has_crispr_gene_effect false}. Corroborated independently inside part A's own quoted record: emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_a_hemcss_identity.cellosaurus.record.DR carries "GDSC; 907290", "Cosmic-CLP; 907290", "Cell_Model_Passport; SIDM00535" and "Omics: Phenotyping; Drug screening". The CRISPR half of the same sentence IS correct (ACH-001519 is absent from part_d.atr_axis_dependency_by_line, 1178 lines). The charitable reading — that "EMC line" silently means "fusion-positive EMC line" — makes the clause circular with the sentence before it and still leaves the DepMap-labelled EMC line's GDSC2 ATRi values unreported.

blockers.summary: THE CRUX, AND IT INVERTS: the paper's one EMC-specific strand reports the structural precondition as SATISFIED where its own producing artifact records NOT_MET for EMC's commonest fusion. The document never prints the word. This is not 'a precondition treated as a phenotype' - it is a precondition that is not met, reported as met.
blockers.evidence: emc-fet-construct-designs.json at the pin carries `constructs[].domains_retained_and_lost.five_prime_FET_half.census_precondition_verdict` for four EMC constructs: EWSR1_NR4A3_type1, EWSR1(1-431), rg_dipeptides_retained 8/30, fraction 0.267 -> 'NOT_MET - the retained segment carries 8 RG dipeptide(s)'; EWSR1_NR4A3_type5, EWSR1(1-472), 11/30, 0.367 -> 'NOT_MET'; EWSR1_NR4A3_type2, EWSR1(1-264), 0/30, 0.0 -> 'PRECONDITION_MET'; TAF15_NR4A3, TAF15(1-161), 0/30, 0.0 -> 'PRECONDITION_MET'. So two of the four modelled EMC fusions fail the precondition, one of them the commonest. Against that: (a) manuscript line 134, the SS0 'who could settle it' table, reads 'Does the mechanism's structural precondition hold for EMC's fusions? | us - in-silico, $0 | OK emc_fet_idr_census.py' - a bare green tick, in a table where every other row whose answer is negative or qualified puts that in the same cell ('OK SS2 - and the answer is no', 'WARN Yes, and not specifically'); (b) the banner, lines 33-34, reads 'The structural census computes, from EMC's own sequence, whether EMC's fusions satisfy the mechanism's precondition - retain the FET N-terminus, lose the RGG repeats. Satisfying a precondition is not carrying the phenotype, so it establishes eligibility for the class claim rather than membership of it' - framing the precondition as satisfied and the only limit as precondition-vs-phenotype; (c) the 'what still stands' table, line 103, renders type 1's 8 of 30 as 'a weaker, non-identical match to the measured construct'; (d) `grep -i 'NOT_MET\|not met'` over the pinned document returns ZERO hits, and 'type 5' appears nowhere. The reader of the banner - the paragraph the document says is 'repeated in every artifact' - is told EMC's fusions satisfy the precondition. FAIRNESS, and it must be in the fix: the census's own `_what_the_controls_calibrate` records that a MEASURED-positive fusion also reads NOT_MET - EWSR1::ATF1 exon 10 retains 8 of 30, fraction 0.267, numerically identical to EMC type 1 - and concludes that 'lose the C-terminal RGG repeats' is satisfied by losing the BULK, 'which makes fraction_of_wildtype_RG_retained the quantity to compare EMC against, and the strict zero-RG verdict a CONSERVATIVE reading'. So NOT_MET does not mean type 1 cannot carry the mechanism. It does mean the printed OK is unsupportable in either direction: on the strict criterion the commonest fusion fails, and on the comparative criterion the precondition is non-discriminating because a fusion the mechanism was measured on fails it too.
blockers.fix: Replace the bare OK at line 134 with the split answer and say which fusion: 'PART - met for type 2 (second-commonest, 0/30 RG); NOT_MET on the same threshold-free criterion for type 1 (commonest, 8/30) and type 5 (11/30)'. In the banner, replace 'whether EMC's fusions satisfy the mechanism's precondition' with the actual state, and add the census's own calibration sentence - that EWSR1::ATF1 exon 10, on which the mechanism WAS measured, retains the same 8 of 30 and also reads NOT_MET, so the strict verdict is conservative and the comparative fraction is the supported quantity. In the 'what still stands' row, print the artifact's verdict word beside the 8 of 30 rather than paraphrasing it as 'a weaker match'. Do NOT resolve this by loosening the census criterion - the calibration note is already the honest resolution and it is already committed.

blockers.quote: What the tier *is*, is a bound on three sides now instead of two: no coordinated dependency, no sensitivity tracking ATM status, and no proliferation-independent DDR signature in EMC tumours.
blockers.summary: Two of the three named 'sides' are readings from instruments this document itself declares incapable of bearing on the hypothesis, so the sentence converts two failed instruments into evidence against the hypothesis, four lines after saying the hypothesis is neither supported nor refuted.
blockers.evidence: Side 1, 'no coordinated dependency', is part C. §4 closes: 'Reported as a failed instrument, and it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis. ... This readout can support the hypothesis or miss it. It cannot refute it.' The artifact agrees — part_c_coordinated_dependency.verdict = 'INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND', verdict_reading = '...this instrument cannot support OR refute a selective ATR-axis dependency in FET-fusion lines.' Side 2, 'no sensitivity tracking ATM status', is part D's ATM row, whose predictor is expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair — transcript abundance. The same §6.1 paragraph, two sentences earlier, says: 'The mechanism is a recruitment-and-phosphorylation event at a double-strand break; nothing in an expression matrix can measure it, so a cell with entirely normal DDR transcript levels can still have a defective ATM response.' Only side 3 (part B, the transcriptional shadow) is a bound the method supports, and §6.1 correctly scopes that one to the shadow. A bound is a partial refutation; the paragraph says in one sentence that no refutation exists and in the next that three of them do. The §6.1 predicate table already prints the honest version of side 1 — 'no — instrument blind (§4)' — so the contradiction is internal to one subsection.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Any restatement that keeps 'bound on three sides' while §4's 'it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis' stands. The two are not reconcilable by hedging the surrounding prose; one of the three sides has to be withdrawn or re-described as an absent reading rather than a null. This is the same distinction the document builds the NOT_ASSESSABLE tier to enforce for part B (§1, §3.3) and then does not enforce for part C in the grading section.

blockers.where: THE HEADLINE (lines 88-91) and §5 throughout; propagated to §6.1's predicate row and to §6.3
blockers.quote: The mechanism's *load-bearing* prediction — **low ATM signalling marks ATRi sensitivity** — comes back at rho = **-0.090**, the **wrong sign** ... [§5] The published mechanism's central variable is still the variable that leaves no trace in this data, on direction and magnitude alike.
blockers.summary: The mechanism's central variable is ATM activation at a double-strand break. It is operationalised here as ATM-pathway transcript abundance, and the failure of that proxy is reported as a fact about the mechanism. §5 nowhere states that an expression matrix cannot observe the variable — and §3.4 attributes that limit TO §5, where it does not exist.
blockers.evidence: grep -n -E 'phosphoryl|recruitment' over the pinned document returns lines 120 (headline, pointing at §6.1), 489 (oxidative phosphorylation, unrelated), 529 (§3.4), 723 (§6.1) and 769 (§6.3). §5 runs from line 590 to line 705 (§6 opens at 706) and contains none of them. Line 529, inside §3.4, reads: 'Section 5's limit applies with full force here: the mechanism is a protein recruitment and phosphorylation event at a double-strand break, and no expression matrix can show it.' — attributing to §5 a limit §5 does not carry. Part B's identical instrument gets the caveat in full and part D's does not, and part D is where the document declares the mechanism not to track. The predictor really is expression: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity['expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair'], mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors = -0.0903, computed from DepMap OmicsExpression log2(TPM+1) over the Reactome DNA Double Strand Break Response set. §5's table row is labelled 'ATM-signalling expression', which is a label rather than a caveat; the headline drops even that. The honest reading of the row is that the instrument cannot see the variable, which is a different finding from the prediction being contradicted — and it changes what §6.1's predicate 'ATR-inhibitor sensitivity tracks the mechanism | no' is a 'no' about.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Restoring 'the wrong sign' as a claim about the mechanism while §6.1 and §3.4 continue to say no expression matrix can measure this event. The fix is one sentence in §5 stating that ATM-pathway transcript level is not ATM signalling capacity, and a correction to §3.4's cross-reference; the headline then has to say the proxy leaves no trace rather than that the prediction comes back wrong. The four bars, the numbers and the 1-of-4 verdict are all untouched by it.

p1s.summary: §2.1 calls PMID 34413129 'a primary source' for the Cellosaurus caution that carries the document's self-declared 'most consequential finding' — but that PMID is an SLFN11 pediatric-sarcoma biomarker study that names H-EMC-SS exactly once, in a Materials-and-Methods cell-line provenance list, and never states a per-line fusion result. The document neither opens it nor tells the reader what it is, so a reader cannot weigh the evidence §2 rests on.
p1s.evidence: The identifier resolves and is transcribed correctly: emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#part_a.cellosaurus.fusion_mentions_verbatim holds the caution byte-for-byte, '(PubMed=34413129)' included, and the sweep records PMID:34413129 as clean. What it resolves TO, fetched from PubMed/PMC: Gartrell J, Mellado-Largarde M, Clay MR, et al., 'SLFN11 is Widely Expressed in Pediatric Sarcoma and Induces Variable Sensitization to Replicative Stress Caused By DNA-Damaging Agents', Mol Cancer Ther 2021;20(11):2151-2165, PMC8571037, doi 10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-21-0089. In its PMC full text (53.5 KB) the string 'H-EMC-SS' occurs ONCE — 'H-EMC-SS (European Collection of Authenticated Cell Cultures, RRID:CVCL_1238)' in the cell-line list — and the words 'myxoid' and 'chondrosarcoma' occur ZERO times. The only methods sentence that could underlie the caution is panel-wide and reports no per-line result: 'Cell lines were authenticated using short tandem repeat analysis via PowerPlex (Promega) and tested for mycoplasma using MycoAlert (Lonza). Translocation status was confirmed using PCR and Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH).' On population provenance the mismatch is explicit: the paper's stated subject is PEDIATRIC sarcoma (220 children), while Cellosaurus records H-EMC-SS as AG 77Y, SX Female — an adult-derived line outside the study's population. ⛔ THIS DOES NOT REFUTE THE CAUTION: the panel-wide PCR/FISH sentence makes a curator-read fusion call plausible, and §2.2's claim is correctly bounded to 'the public record does not support' with an explicit ⛔ list of what is NOT established, so the bounded claim survives. What fails is the characterisation, and it fails in the direction that flatters the finding.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Replace 'citing a primary source' with what the source is and what it does and does not report — e.g. 'citing Gartrell et al., Mol Cancer Ther 2021;20:2151-2165 (PMID 34413129), a pediatric-sarcoma SLFN11 study that used H-EMC-SS in its panel and states only panel-wide that translocation status was confirmed by PCR and FISH; no per-line fusion result appears in its text.' Any edit that keeps the phrase 'primary source' without naming the paper leaves the reader unable to weigh §2, and any edit that asserts the paper characterised H-EMC-SS reintroduces a claim its retrievable text does not carry.

p1s.summary: §6.3 states that for SRP640302 'the sample sizes and fusion annotation are unknown until it is opened' — this repository opened it on 2026-08-08, three and a half weeks before the pin, and committed both the measurement and the deposit's publication. §6.3 also names SRP445369 under the header 'EMC RNA-seq quantified from raw reads', but that study's own deposited name is a WHOLE-GENOME study, from which no expression matrix can be quantified.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-sra-study.json (_generated_utc 2026-08-08T20:25:51Z): target_sra_study SRP640302, target_bioproject PRJNA1357027, resolved true for both, pairing_check verdict CONSISTENT, transport_gate_passed true, verdict.grade EMC_PUBLIC_CANDIDATE with headline 'an EMC deposit with 12 runs over 12 samples is public and downloadable; library strategy ["RNA-Seq"]', n_runs_measured 12, n_distinct_samples_measured 12, assay_probe_matched_text 'TempO-Seq'. research/literature/emc-fourth-cohort-publication-2026-08-24.json names the deposit's publication: PMID 42465974, doi 10.7717/peerj.21497, 'Prognostic biomarkers for enhanced risk stratification in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma: a retrospective cohort study', abstract 'We performed whole-transcriptome targeted RNA sequencing (TempO-Seq) on archiv[ed FFPE]', n = 12 FFPE, 6/6 prognosis split, with a whole characterisation manuscript at research/manuscripts/fusion-output/emc-fourth-cohort-sra-2026-08-08.md. systems/graph/blockers.json adds 'downloadable since 2025-11-11, carrying per-sample EWSR1 break-apart FISH status' — i.e. the fusion annotation §6.3 calls unknown is recorded as present. On the second half: the ATR document's own artifact (emc-atr-vulnerability.json → part_b.dataset_search.sra.studies) records SRP445369's name verbatim as 'Whole Genome Sequencing for Metastatic Mutational Burden in Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma'. Consequences for the sentence as written: 'alignment and quantification from FASTQ' is the wrong pipeline for a TempO-Seq probe deposit (the repo's own emc_fourth_cohort_quant.py does probe-count matching, not transcriptome alignment), and the ATR document names neither PRJNA1357027 nor PMID 42465974, so a reader cannot cross-walk to the characterisation that already exists.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Replace the §6.3 row's 'the sample sizes and fusion annotation are unknown until it is opened' with the measured state and a pointer — n = 12 runs over 12 samples, whole-transcriptome targeted TempO-Seq (Chaiboonchoe et al., PeerJ 2026, PMID 42465974, doi 10.7717/peerj.21497), BioProject PRJNA1357027, characterised in emc-fourth-cohort-sra-2026-08-08.md — and drop SRP445369 from a row headed 'EMC RNA-seq quantified from raw reads' or relabel it as the whole-genome deposit it is. Any edit that keeps 'unknown' while this repository holds emc-sra-study.json restates a claim its own committed record falsifies.

p1s.summary: The Bangerter reference is printed with two different years in one document — §2.2 gives 'Hum Cell 2023;36:446-455', the Appendix gives 'Hum Cell 2022;36:446-455' — on the single sourced epidemiological bound (>90 % NR4A3 rearrangement) that stops §2.2 reading as a reclassification of a real cell line. Every fetched record in this repository, the document's own inputs cache included, says 2023.
p1s.evidence: At the pin, line 247-248 (§2.2): 'Bangerter et al., *Hum Cell* 2023;36:446-455, [PMID 36316541], [doi:10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x]'. Line 1028 (Appendix): 'Bangerter et al., *Hum Cell* 2022;36:446-455, [PMID 36316541]'. PubMed for 36316541 returns journal 'Human cell', volume 36, issue 1, pages 446-455, with publication_date 2022-11-01 (the Epub) — so volume 36 issue 1 is the 2023 print issue and 2023 is the citable year. The document's own emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json → part_a.literature records that PMID with year '2023'; research/literature/submission-reference-metadata-2026-08-09.json records year 2023, volume 36, issue 1, pages 446-455, PMC9813045; two sibling manuscripts' reference lists (emc-fusion-partner-stratification.md [12], emc-surface-target-landscape.md) both write 2023. The '2022' matches only the DOI's own year segment (s13577-022-00818-x). The QUOTATION itself is exact against PubMed's abstract: 'EMCs are translocation sarcomas and harbor in > 90% of the cases an NR4A3 rearrangement.' This is the document's own recurring one-of-a-pair defect — the correction reached §2.2 and not its neighbour in the Appendix, which is the third instance the Appendix already records for other numbers.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Set both occurrences to 'Hum Cell 2023;36(1):446-455', matching every committed record. Any edit that leaves 2022 beside PMID 36316541 reintroduces the conflict with submission-reference-metadata-2026-08-09.json and with the document's own inputs cache.

p1s.summary: §6.1 asserts the fixed WEAK criterion is met "verbatim" and "precisely", and neither series satisfies it as written. On the series that actually carries the verdict, two UNRELATED control sets clear the same elevation cut — so it is not "only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes" that are elevated; on the second series NOTHING clears the cut, so it does not show generic elevation either. Row 1 of the same four-row table states the contradicting fact. This is the one section whose stated purpose is that the criteria cannot be softened after the fact, and the producing module's own `why` string carries the disjunct the prose drops.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript §6.1 predicate table row 4: "Only generic proliferation / DNA-damage genes are elevated | yes — which is the WEAK criterion, verbatim", and the paragraph below it: "The verbatim WEAK criterion is 'only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes are elevated', and that is precisely what two independent EMC series show." Against emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature: unrelated_control_concepts_elevated = ["control_adipogenesis", "control_oxphos"], i.e. TWO sets that are neither proliferation nor DNA-damage clear §1's own >0.2 cut (pooled_raw_contrast: control_oxphos +0.3843 t 3.952, control_adipogenesis +0.2183 t 5.081 — oxphos is the LARGEST mover of any concept scored). The pooled read is GSE4303/GPL3290 alone (every pooled_raw_contrast entry has n_platforms 1; platforms_with_a_readable_EMC_vs_comparator_contrast lists that one file; series_carrying_the_verdict "GSE4303"). On the concordance series the same cut is cleared by nothing at all: per_platform["GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz"].contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma has proliferation_MYC +0.0844, control_oxphos +0.1131, every DDR concept |delta| <= 0.0445. §3.4 states the contradicting fact plainly ("the two unrelated control sets (oxphos, adipogenesis) move as much as or more than any DDR set"), as does §6.1's own row 1. The artifact's grading.why keeps the qualifier the prose loses: "… the DDR concepts do not survive adjustment for proliferation, OR unrelated control sets move with them", and emc_atr_vulnerability.py computes the predicate as `bool(sig_present and sig_specific is False)`, not from the criterion's words. The tier itself is not disputed — WEAK is the closest of the three and the module's own output — only the claim that the criterion is met verbatim.

p1s.summary: §1 says "A fourth outcome exists and is not in the fixed list, so it is named rather than folded into one of the three: NOT_ASSESSABLE." The producing module carries a FIFTH outcome outside the fixed list — MODERATE_PLUS — which the manuscript never names anywhere. The enumeration is the point of that paragraph: it is what tells a reader the outcome space was fixed in advance and is completely disclosed.
p1s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py, grade(): the tier branches are STRONG, WEAK, MODERATE, MODERATE_PLUS and NOT_ASSESSABLE. MODERATE_PLUS's own why string is "The signature holds and one of the two surrogate mechanism tests supports it, but not both, so the STRONG conjunction is not met. Reported between the fixed tiers rather than rounded up to STRONG." `grep -n MODERATE` over the pinned manuscript returns exactly one line — line 154, the verbatim MODERATE criterion — and no occurrence of MODERATE_PLUS. Its omission does not flatter the result (MODERATE_PLUS is a refusal to round up), which is why this is a disclosure defect rather than a grading one.

p1s.summary: §6.1 uses part C as one of three sides of a bound, which §4 forbids in terms. §4 ends "it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis … This readout can support the hypothesis or miss it. It cannot refute it"; §6.1 then writes "a bound on three sides now instead of two: no coordinated dependency, no sensitivity tracking ATM status, and no proliferation-independent DDR signature". A blind instrument's null is an absent reading, and counting it as a bound is the exact collapse §1 built the NOT_ASSESSABLE tier to refuse — applied to part B and not to part C.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript §4 closing paragraph vs §6.1 paragraph 2. emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_c_coordinated_dependency.verdict "INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND", verdict_reading "… this instrument cannot support OR refute a selective ATR-axis dependency in FET-fusion lines. Reported as a failed instrument", and knockout_instrument_with_matched_comparator._criterion defines blindness as the axis sitting at the common-essential floor with the between-group delta smaller than the within-group SD (axis_mean_sarcoma_pool -1.34, axis_sd_sarcoma_pool 0.1904, delta_FET_minus_matched -0.0065, frac_lines_dependent_on_axis_sarcoma_pool 1.0). The same section's predicate row also answers "Other FET-fusion models show selective ATR-pathway dependency" with "no — instrument blind (§4)"; that rendering is defensible for a predicate meaning 'was it shown', but the prose then converts it into an evidential bound, which is not.

p1s.summary: The headline calls the one passing mechanism test "two instruments agreeing about the same target"; §5 says in terms that the agreement is at MODULE level rather than at target level, that the predictor is a three-gene mean, and that nothing in the analysis separates ATR from a neighbouring checkpoint kinase. The correction landed in §5 and not in the summary that a reader takes away — the one-of-a-pair shape this document's own Appendix records three times.
p1s.evidence: Headline: "the one that passes is a statement about the drug rather than about EMC (lines more ATR-dependent by CRISPR are more ATR-inhibitor-sensitive — two instruments agreeing about the same target)". §5: "This is an internal-consistency check passing, at MODULE level rather than at target level", "no bar in this analysis separates ATR from a neighbouring checkpoint kinase". The predictor is emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity["dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect"] — a mean gene effect over three genes, not one target — and its per_drug_rho_near_neighbour_DDR records mk-1775 (WEE1i) at rho +0.1571 (t 3.893, n 601) against berzosertib's +0.1726 (t 4.157, n 565), with no interval computed for either.

p1s.summary: The headline's "what still stands" table sources the two-fusion RG bracket to emc_fet_idr_census.py, and that artifact contains only ONE EMC fusion, labels it `emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3`, and runs its whole comparative verdict on that label — the exact drift the Appendix says was flagged on 2026-08-03 and corrected. The prose is right and the census pointer is stale: the type-1 numbers the row prints exist only in the sibling construct-designs artifact, and the census's headline claim is true of type 2 and false of the fusion the paper calls EMC's actual commonest.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript headline table row 1 cites "emc_fet_idr_census.py and emc_fet_construct_designs.py" for "type 2 … EWSR1(1-264) … 0 of 30; type 1 (EWSR1 exon 12::NR4A3 exon 3, the actual commonest EMC fusion) retains EWSR1(1-431) and keeps 8 of 30". emc-fet-idr-census.json holds exactly one EMC record, `emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3` = {last_fet_residue_retained 264, rg_dipeptides_retained 0, fraction_of_wildtype_RG_retained 0.0, breakpoint_provenance "EWSR1 transcript exon 7"}; the string "431" does not occur anywhere in the file (grep -c = 0). Its emc_vs_measured_fusions_comparative._claim_under_test is "EMC's canonical fusion loses at least as much of EWSR1's RGG content as each fusion in which ATM suppression was MEASURED" with holds_against_every_measured_type true — true at 0.0 for type 2, false for type 1 at 0.267 against EWSR1::FLI1 (0.0) and EWSR1::ATF1 e8 (0.233). The type-1 figures ARE sourced: emc-fet-construct-designs.json -> constructs[0].junction_in_residue_numbering.five_prime_residues_fully_encoded = 431 and rgg_dose_calibration_and_predictions.emc_constructs_on_the_same_axis type 1 = {rg_dipeptides_retained 8, fraction 0.267}. The Appendix's own standing lesson applies to the copy that remains: "A correction is not applied until every copy has been searched for by string."

p1s.summary: The census artifact still calls EMC's SECOND-commonest fusion 'canonical' and runs the whole comparative claim on it, so the claim the paper cites as its EMC-specific strand does not cover the commonest fusion and would invert for it. The manuscript's own Appendix says this label drift was flagged 2026-08-03 and corrected 'this hardening round' - the correction reached the prose and not the artifact.
p1s.evidence: emc-fet-idr-census.json at the pin has exactly one EMC entry, keyed `emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3`, holding EWSR1(1-264) / 0 of 30 RG / precondition_met true. `grep -c 431` over the whole census returns 0: the commonest fusion is not in it at all. `emc_vs_measured_fusions_comparative._claim_under_test` reads "EMC's canonical fusion loses at least as much of EWSR1's RGG content as each fusion in which ATM suppression was MEASURED", with emc_RG_retained_fraction 0.0 on all four rows and `holds_against_every_measured_type: true`. Substituting type 1's 0.267 (from emc-fet-construct-designs.json) against the two comparator rows at 0.0 - EWSR1::FLI1 type 1 and EWSR1::ATF1 exon 7 - gives 0.267 > 0.0, so `emc_loses_at_least_as_much` is false on two of four rows and `holds_against_every_measured_type` would be false. Manuscript SS7 states 'nothing is hand-typed here that the artifact does not carry'; the type-1 numbers are carried (by the construct-designs artifact) but the type-1 VERDICT and the type-1 comparative result are carried by nothing.
p1s.fix: Rekey the census entry off 'canonical' and add type 1 (and type 5) to it, so the comparative block reports per-type rather than for one type under a label the manuscript has already retired. Until that regeneration lands, the manuscript must not cite `emc_fet_idr_census.py` as the home of a statement about 'EMC's fusions' plural.

p1s.summary: SS2.1 argues from NR4A3 expression against the fusion using exactly the inference SS8.3 rules out - and the limit is stated in SS8.3 and absent in SS2, which the document itself calls 'the most consequential finding in the document'.
p1s.evidence: SS8.3 principle 1, verbatim: 'The index has no fusion entry. An EWSR1::NR4A3 transcript is EWSR1 exons 1-12 joined to NR4A3 exon 3. Against a wild-type transcript index, junction-spanning reads map cleanly to neither entry and the EWSR1-derived 5' half never counts toward NR4A3 at all - so a fusion's contribution to an NR4A3 TPM is systematically under-counted.' DepMap OmicsExpression is also a wild-type-index quantification. SS2.1 nonetheless writes: 'a line whose driver transcript carries the NR4A3 body under EWSR1's promoter would be expected to read far higher', and grades the observed value 'Weak corroboration only' - i.e. weak evidence AGAINST the fusion. Second half: SS8.3 introduces NR4A3/(NR4A1+NR4A2+NR4A3) as 'the ratio that survives' the index confound and reports it for the USZ model (0.0634, rank 29 of 68, panel median 0.0524). The identical three inputs for H-EMC-SS sit in the same artifact - `part_a_hemcss_identity.depmap_expression` gives NR4A3 0.941, NR4A1 3.025, NR4A2 0.202 in log2(TPM+1) - and the same statistic is never computed there. Computed here from those artifact values it is 0.112, with NR4A1 outweighing NR4A3 7.8x, the same qualitative pattern SS8.3 reports for the USZ model and does not report for this one. Recorded as an unrun check, not as a claim about the line's identity: the two panels are normalised differently and the numbers are not comparable across them.
p1s.fix: Carry SS8.3's index-under-counting sentence into SS2.1, beside the 'would be expected to read far higher' claim, and either run the family-fraction check on H-EMC-SS or state why it is not run. SS2's verdict rests on Cellosaurus plus the filtered fusion caller and does not move either way - which is the reason to say so explicitly rather than leave an expression argument standing that the paper's own later section disowns.

p1s.summary: The class the vulnerability is inherited from is counted two different ways in the same document - two fusions in the banner, four diseases in SS8.2 - and the census's positive-control set covers half of it, never testing a non-EWSR1 FET protein.
p1s.evidence: Banner, line 26: 'the two the structural census carries as positive controls are EWSR1::FLI1 (Ewing) and EWSR1::ATF1 (clear cell sarcoma)'. SS8.2: 'Ewing sarcoma, clear cell sarcoma, DSRCT and myxoid liposarcoma - every FET-fusion sarcoma the mechanism this route rests on was measured in'. The committed cache settles it and supports the LARGER set: atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json#mechanism_fulltext_xml gives the source's cell-line panel verbatim as '4 ES cell lines with varying TP53 and STAG2 status ..., 1 CCS (EWSR1-ATF1), 2 desmoplastic small round cell tumor (EWSR1-WT1), and 1 myxoid liposarcoma cell line (FUS-CHOP), and multiple non-FET rearranged cancer cell lines as controls', its PDX panel as 'Elimusertib was tested in 5 PDX models: 2 ES models ..., 2 CCS models ..., and 1 desmoplastic small round cell tumor (DSRCT) PDX', and states 'we also verified that the DSRCT fusion EWSR1-WT1 is recruited to laser-induced DSBs with similar kinetics to EWSR1-FLI and EWSR1-ATF1'. So the mechanism was measured on four FET fusions across four diseases, one of them FUS-CHOP - a FUS fusion, not EWSR1. emc-fet-idr-census.json's `_control_rule` says the controls are 'the fusions the mechanism was measured on' and carries two, both EWSR1, so the census's operational definitions (EWSR1's 30 RG dipeptides, the residue-299 RGG-free ceiling) are never calibrated against a different FET protein - and EMC's own minority partners include TAF15 and FUS, which the paper sweeps.
p1s.fix: Make the banner's count match SS8.2's and match the source: four measured fusions, four diseases. Add EWSR1::WT1 and FUS::CHOP to the census's positive controls and report whether the precondition's definitions recover their architecture - a control set that omits the only non-EWSR1 measured fusion cannot tell you whether the definition generalises across the family it is being applied to.

p1s.summary: Part D's stated instrument limitation is contradicted by an existence proof sitting in the document's own committed cache, and the compound the source paper actually advanced is named nowhere in the manuscript.
p1s.evidence: SS5: 'PRISM was attempted and did not become available. The DepMap portal's file index did not return parsable JSON; the quarterly figshare releases were already measured to carry no drug matrix. GDSC2 is therefore the only drug-response instrument here - a limitation, not a choice.' The cached source full text (atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json#mechanism_fulltext_xml) carries a figure legend reading 'Analysis of DepMap Elimusertib sensitivity scores with samples divided into Ewing sarcoma (ES) and non-ES samples' - i.e. the paper this route rests on published a DepMap ATR-inhibitor sensitivity analysis, for elimusertib, the compound it used in vitro (ES IC50s 28 and 34 nM; CCS 27 nM) and in all 5 PDX models. `grep -c -i elimusertib` over the pinned manuscript returns 0. Part D's ATR-inhibitor set is ceralasertib and berzosertib only.
p1s.fix: Name elimusertib, say it is absent from GDSC2 8.5, and state that a DepMap elimusertib sensitivity readout demonstrably exists because the source paper analysed one - so the SS5 sentence is about this programme's fetch route failing, not about the instrument not existing. SS6.3 already lists 'a drug-response instrument that is not GDSC2 (PRISM, if it becomes fetchable)' as a grade-mover; the existence proof belongs in that row.

p1s.summary: The proliferation control that decides three of four part-D tests, and the WEAK-tier predicate, is MYC Targets V1 - and MYC-driven oncogene-induced replication stress is the competing mechanism the source paper had to exclude experimentally. 'Cannot beat the proliferation control' may therefore mean 'cannot beat a second replication-stress axis', not 'is only growth rate'.
p1s.evidence: SS1 and SS3.2: the proliferation controls are Hallmark Myc Targets V1 (200) and Mitotic Spindle (199); the part-D bar is `abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15` against `expr::proliferation_MYC` at rho -0.1711; the part-B adjustment subtracts each sample's own proliferation score; the fixed grading's WEAK tier is 'only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes are elevated'. The cached source text frames the same axis as mechanism, not nuisance: 'Previously described mechanisms of ATR sensitivity, most notably replication stress (RS), could also contribute to the elimusertib effects that we observed. To test this directly, we expressed RNAseH1, which degrades R-loops, the major source of oncogene-induced replication stress in ES'. The manuscript addresses only gene-membership overlap between the DDR concepts and the proliferation union (ATR-CHK1 9 of 37 = 24.3 %, S-phase/E2F 54 of 200 = 27.0 %, checkpoint 68 of 200 = 34.0 %, against 2.0-6.5 % for the unrelated controls) - a set-overlap argument, which is a different objection from the control being mechanistically loaded. Note also that this control tracks berzosertib at rho -0.2454, larger in magnitude than the passing dependency predictor's berzosertib value of +0.1726.
p1s.fix: State the objection where the bar is defined (SS1) and where it decides (SS5, SS6.1): a MYC-target set is not a mechanism-neutral nuisance variable for an ATR hypothesis, because oncogene-induced replication stress is itself a nominated ATR-inhibitor sensitivity axis and the source paper treats it as one. Either add a proliferation control that is not MYC-anchored - Mitotic Spindle alone is already computed - or say plainly that the bar as built cannot separate the mechanism from a second replication-stress axis, which weakens the negative rather than the positive.

p1s.summary: The mechanism's load-bearing predictor is a transcript proxy for a post-translational lesion. The paper states that limit twice for part B and never at the point in part D where it draws its conclusion from the proxy - and the field-standard instrument for the same question, ATM genetic status, is available at $0, unused, and unnamed.
p1s.evidence: SS3.4: 'the mechanism is a protein recruitment and phosphorylation event at a double-strand break, and no expression matrix can show it. A cell can have wholly normal DDR transcript levels and a wholly defective ATM response.' SS6.1 repeats it. SS5 then implements 'low ATM signalling' as a Reactome DNA Double Strand Break Response expression score (61 genes), reports rho -0.0903, and concludes 'The published mechanism's central variable is still the variable that leaves no trace in this data, on direction and magnitude alike' - the mechanism's central variable named as measured, in the one section the transcript caveat is absent from. Separately, `grep -i 'ATM mutation\|ATM loss\|ATM protein\|ATM-deficient\|mutation status\|copy number\|proteom'` over the pinned document returns nothing: DepMap carries ATM mutation and copy-number calls for the same models part D maps to GDSC2, ATM loss-of-function is the field's standard ATR-inhibitor-sensitivity stratifier, and the source paper's own comparator for its elimusertib IC50s is 'cancer cell lines with known pathogenic ATM loss of function mutations'. SS6.3's 'what would move the grade' names no such analysis.
p1s.fix: Carry the transcript caveat into SS5 beside the ATM row and re-word the conclusion to say the mechanism's central variable was proxied by transcripts, not measured. Add an ATM-genetic-status stratification of the same GDSC2 residuals to SS6.3 as a $0 self-doable mover - it is the test a DNA-damage-response referee will ask for first, and its absence is more damaging than the wrong-sign correlation it would replace.

p1s.summary: The single passing test has no same-modality negative control. Nothing in part D tests whether ANY strong CRISPR dependency score correlates with the ATR-inhibitor residual, so 'ATR-axis dependency predicts ATRi sensitivity' is not separated from 'dependency scores in general predict drug-specific residuals'.
p1s.evidence: part_d_drug_response_correlation.correlations carries 10 predictors x 7 drugs = 70 Spearman correlations. Exactly one predictor is a dependency score: dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect. Its two specificity bars compare it against EXPRESSION predictors (expr::proliferation_MYC at rho -0.1711) and against non-DDR DRUGS (paclitaxel +0.007, bortezomib +0.0213). No pan-essential or unrelated-gene dependency predictor exists. The module's own comment concedes the cross-modal problem — 'a dependency predictor is on a different scale and sign from an expression predictor, so the comparison is on |rho| and is only meaningful as "is this bigger than growth rate"' — and the paper reproduces the scale caveat once, in its standard-error sentence. The missing control is free: RPL5 (-2.7439) and PLK1 (-2.7148) gene effects are already computed and cached in the SAME artifact, part_c_coordinated_dependency.per_gene, and part D already reads CRISPRGeneEffect. A pan-essential dependency score correlated against the same seven drugs is the one comparison that would tell a reader whether the passing row is about ATR or about line fitness — which is the document's own thesis for everything else it reports.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing in the text; the gap is in the analysis. Absent that control, §5's '✅ What passes, and why it is worth something' has to state that the passing predictor's negative control is cross-modal and that no dependency-modality null was run.

p1s.where: §3.4, the sentence carrying part B's conclusion; repeated in §6.1's predicate table
p1s.quote: Three DDR concepts clear the raw threshold and none survives the proliferation adjustment — and the two *unrelated* control sets (oxphos, adipogenesis) move as much as or more than any DDR set. That is the signature of a growth-rate difference, not of a DDR mechanism.
p1s.summary: False for one of the two controls, and refuted by the table eight lines above it. Only oxphos exceeds every DDR set; adipogenesis is exceeded by three of them. The 'growth rate, not DDR' reading is carried by one control, not two.
p1s.evidence: From per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'].contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma, raw delta_a_minus_b: control_adipogenesis +0.2183, against ATR_CHK1_activity +0.2451, DNA_damage_checkpoint +0.2564 and S_phase_E2F +0.3111. control_oxphos +0.3843 does exceed all six DDR concepts. The paper prints all of these numbers in its own §3.4 table. On the proliferation-adjusted scale the gap widens: adipogenesis +0.0353 against S_phase_E2F +0.1282 and DNA_damage_checkpoint +0.0735. §6.1 restates it as 'two unrelated control sets move as much (§3.4)'. Read charitably as 'at least as much as SOME DDR set' the sentence is true and vacuous; in the position it occupies, immediately before 'That is the signature of a growth-rate difference', it is doing the work of 'at least as much as ALL of them', and that is false for adipogenesis on both scales.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any restatement that keeps both controls in the comparison. The claim that survives is the one-control version — oxidative phosphorylation, an unrelated control, moves further than every DDR concept — plus the adjustment result, which stands on its own.

p1s.where: §6.1, and §3.4's 'it does not matter here, because the two series agree'
p1s.quote: The verbatim WEAK criterion is *"only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes are elevated"*, and that is precisely what two independent EMC series show.
p1s.summary: The graded predicate reads ONE series. On the other, nothing at all clears the elevation cut — DDR, proliferation and controls alike — so the WEAK criterion's own words are not instantiated there, and the module's verdict for that series alone would be the string §3.3 records as the near-published failure.
p1s.evidence: part_b_emc_tumour_signature.platforms_with_a_readable_EMC_vs_comparator_contrast = ['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'], a single entry, and every row of pooled_raw_contrast carries n_platforms: 1. GSE24369 appears in readable_platforms_in_ANY_series and contributes to no predicate. Run the module's own cut over GSE24369's contrasts: the largest |delta| across all twelve concepts is control_oxphos +0.1131; proliferation_MYC is +0.0844 and no DDR concept exceeds +0.0445. Nothing reaches 0.2, so ddr_concepts_elevated_raw would be empty, signature_present would be False, and derive_part_b's first branch would set verdict = 'NO_DDR_SIGNATURE_IN_EMC_TUMOURS' with the reading 'that is a readable negative, and it is evidence against the transfer' — the exact sentence §3.3 records as the failure the module exists to prevent — rather than 'GENERIC_ONLY'. grade() would still land on WEAK, but through its final else branch ('the grading's leading predicate fails'), not through the 'only generic ... elevated' branch. So the two series reach the same tier by different routes and do not show the same thing; and §3.4's 'it does not matter here, because the two series agree', which is what defuses the rank-key choice, is weaker than stated. This matters because the series the rank key DID pick is the one §3.4 itself calls 'not the better instrument' and the one carrying the undetermined reference-channel confound.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Keeping 'precisely what two independent EMC series show'. The supported version is that GSE24369 is flat at every concept including the generic ones, which is consistent with the WEAK reading and is not an instance of it.

p1s.quote: [§8.4] SARC-HRD would not select it at all if EMC is HR-proficient as its class is measured to be. ... [§8.2] If EMC behaves as its class does — HR-proficient, per the source paper's own measurement on the FET class —
p1s.summary: Both sentences assert a class-level measurement of HR status. §8.5, thirty lines later, denies it: the measurement was on Ewing tumours. Measured on one member, asserted of the class — the elision the banner exists to forbid, inside the section that draws the adverse consequence for route 1.
p1s.evidence: §8.5 point 1 reads in full: 'That EMC is HR-proficient. Not measured here. The source paper measured it for *Ewing* tumours, and EMC's HR status is unknown in public data.' The preprint quotations §8.2 itself reproduces are all scoped to ES: 'ES patient tumors do not display the genomic scars of HR deficiency', 'EWSR1-FLI1 does not induce isolated HR deficiency', 'ES tumors are not "BRCA-like", but instead harbor partial ATM defects'. The only class-level statement in the quoted material is a NOMINATION — 'identify the compensatory ATR signaling axis as a synthetic lethal therapeutic strategy for the class of FET rearranged cancers' — which is a claim by the authors, not a measurement across the class. The banner's own rule applies verbatim: the mechanism 'was measured on other FET fusions in other diseases', and class inheritance is not a measurement.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any wording that keeps 'as its class is measured to be' or 'measurement on the FET class'. The supported form is 'as measured in Ewing', which is what §8.5 already says and which weakens neither of §8.4's three findings — none of them needs EMC to be HR-proficient, only that its HR status is unknown.
